title: My plans after university
paragraphs: My name is Aliya Serikova. I am twenty years old and I come from Taraz, in the south of Kazakhstan. I study Medicine at WKU — it is my third year, and graduation is only two years away. People often say that the third year is the hardest in Medicine, and I agree. But it is also the most exciting, because for the first time I can see the end of the road ahead of me. I know what I want. And I have a clear plan for what I am going to do.

My first plan is the most immediate: after I graduate, I am going to do a one-year internship here in Uralsk. WKU has a strong connection with the Regional Clinical Hospital, and I am going to apply for their internship programme next spring. The internship is going to be intensive and demanding — I am going to work in three different departments: general medicine, paediatrics, and emergency care. It is going to be hard. But I am going to learn more in that one year than in any year of university.

After the internship, I am going to move back to my hometown of Taraz. My plan is to work at the Regional Hospital there — the same hospital where my mother has worked as a nurse for twenty-two years. Taraz is a beautiful city, and it needs more doctors. I am not going to work in Almaty or Astana — the big cities already have enough medical professionals. My community is going to benefit more from my work. That matters to me.

In three or four years, after I have some experience as a doctor, I am going to apply for a Master's degree in Public Health. I am going to study the health systems of different countries and learn how to improve healthcare for communities. I am not going to do this immediately after university — I want to work first, understand real problems, and then study solutions. A Master's degree with real clinical experience behind it is going to be much more valuable than one without.

On a personal level, I am going to visit my grandmother in Shymkent every month. She is seventy-eight years old and she lives alone, and being close to family is very important to me. I am also going to save money carefully — my goal is to have enough for a small apartment in Taraz within five years. I am not going to buy a new phone or travel abroad for holidays. I am going to invest in things that last.

One thing I am definitely NOT going to do is leave Kazakhstan permanently. I hear many students talking about going to work in other countries — Germany, Canada, the UAE. I understand their reasons. But Kazakhstan is my country, and it needs doctors who stay. Every young doctor who leaves is a loss for the people here. I am going to be part of the solution, not part of the problem. That is my biggest plan — and my biggest promise to myself.

dialogue.speaker: Dinara
dialogue.text: Aliya, you're in your third year now. Have you thought about what you're going to do after graduation?

dialogue.speaker: Aliya
dialogue.text: Yes, a lot! First, I'm going to do a one-year internship here in Uralsk at the Regional Hospital.

dialogue.speaker: Dinara
dialogue.text: Are you going to stay in Uralsk after the internship?

dialogue.speaker: Aliya
dialogue.text: No — after the internship, I'm going to move back to Taraz and work at the hospital there.

dialogue.speaker: Dinara
dialogue.text: And are you going to do a Master's degree? I know you mentioned it once.

dialogue.speaker: Aliya
dialogue.text: Yes, but not immediately. I'm going to work for three or four years first — then apply.

dialogue.speaker: Dinara
dialogue.text: Are you going to leave Kazakhstan for your Master's? Germany, maybe?

dialogue.speaker: Aliya
dialogue.text: No. I'm not going to leave Kazakhstan. This country needs doctors who stay and work here.

dialogue.speaker: Dinara
dialogue.text: What about personal plans? Are you going to travel or anything?

dialogue.speaker: Aliya
dialogue.text: I'm going to visit my grandmother in Shymkent every month. And I'm going to save for an apartment.

dialogue.speaker: Dinara
dialogue.text: You have such a clear plan! I'm not going to lie — I'm a bit jealous!

dialogue.speaker: Aliya
dialogue.text: You have time! What are YOU going to do after WKU?
